title: Asado (Uruguayan wood-fired beef barbecue)

ingredients.name: beef short ribs (tira de asado), cut across the bone in strips
hardwood lump charcoal or wood for embers
white vinegar and 2 tbsp oil for a salsa criolla

steps: Light the wood or charcoal about 45 minutes ahead, in one side of the grill, and let it burn down to glowing grey embers rather than flames.
Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and salt it generously with the coarse salt just before it goes on the grill.
Set the grill rack about 20 cm above a small bed of embers, shovelling more embers beneath as needed so the heat stays gentle.
Place the short ribs bone side down first and cook for 45 minutes to 1 hour, then turn and cook the other side for another 30 minutes until browned and tender.
Add the sausages for the last 30 minutes, turning until evenly browned and cooked through.
Mix the tomato, onion, vinegar, oil and a little salt into a fresh salsa criolla and let it stand while the meat cooks.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes, then carve and serve with lemon wedges, the salsa and bread.

title: Budín de pan (Uruguayan caramel bread pudding)
steps: Soak the torn bread in the milk for 30 minutes until soft, then squeeze lightly and mash with a fork.

Heat the oven to 180 C. Melt the caramel sugar in a small pan over medium heat, without stirring, until it is a deep amber, then pour it into a 22 cm loaf or ring mould and tilt to coat the base and sides.
Beat the eggs with the pudding sugar, vanilla and zest, then mix thoroughly into the bread with the raisins.
Pour the mixture into the caramelised mould and set it in a roasting dish. Pour hot water into the dish to come halfway up the mould.
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour until set and a knife comes out clean.
Cool completely, run a knife around the edge and turn the pudding out so the caramel runs over it. Serve at room temperature or chilled, optionally with dulce de leche.

title: Capeletis a la Caruso (cappelletti in Uruguayan cream, ham and mushroom sauce)

ingredients.name: beef bouillon paste or stock concentrate
grated parmesan or similar hard cheese

steps: Melt the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and they begin to brown, then stir in the ham.
Sprinkle with flour and stir for a minute, then pour in the cream, stirring, with the bouillon paste.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens, then add the walnuts, a pinch of nutmeg and pepper and taste for salt.
Cook the cappelletti in plenty of salted boiling water according to the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes, and drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce for a minute so it is well coated, and serve with grated cheese on top.

title: Churros rellenos (Uruguayan churros filled with dulce de leche)
steps: Bring the water, butter and salt to a boil in a saucepan, then tip in the flour all at once and stir vigorously until a smooth dough forms and pulls away from the sides.
Cool the dough for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until glossy and smooth.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star nozzle.
Heat 5 cm of oil to about 175 C. Pipe 12 cm lengths into the oil, cutting them off with scissors, and fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and roll in the sugar while still warm.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a narrow nozzle with the dulce de leche and push the tip into the end of each churro to fill it. Serve warm.

title: Dulce de batata (Uruguayan sweet potato jelly)

ingredients.name: orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed

steps: Boil the sweet potato cubes in water until completely soft, about 15 minutes, drain and puree until very smooth.
Heat the sugar with the 150 ml of water, orange peel and cinnamon until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 5 minutes to make a syrup.
Remove the peel and cinnamon and stir the sweet potato puree into the syrup.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 30 to 40 minutes, until the mixture is thick enough that you can see the bottom of the pot when you drag the spoon across it.
Stir in the vanilla and lemon juice, then pour into a lined dish or mould and smooth the top.
Cool completely and chill until firm, then cut into slices and serve with fresh cheese or on its own.

title: Matambre relleno (Uruguayan stuffed rolled flank steak)

ingredients.name: flank steak, butterflied to an even thin sheet (matambre)
carrots, cooked until just tender and sliced lengthwise

steps: Lay the flank steak flat, pound it to an even thickness and rub it with garlic, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper.
Spread the spinach over the meat, leaving a 2 cm border, and arrange the carrot sticks, roasted pepper strips and whole eggs in lines along the length.
Roll the meat up tightly like a roulade and tie it securely with kitchen string at 3 cm intervals, or sew the seam.
Put the roll in a snug pot, add the milk and enough water to nearly cover, and simmer very gently for 1.5 hours.
Lift out the matambre, place it in a baking dish and roast at 200 C for 20 minutes to brown the surface.
Cool completely, ideally pressed under a weight in the fridge for several hours, then cut into 1 cm slices to show the spiral of stuffing.
Serve cold with salad or mayonnaise, or warm with the cooking juices.

title: Pamplona (Uruguayan stuffed chicken roll for the grill)

ingredients.name: large chicken breast fillets (about 600 g), butterflied and pounded thin
mozzarella or other melting cheese, in sticks

steps: Season the flattened chicken with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano.
Lay slices of ham on each fillet and place a stick of cheese and a strip of roasted pepper along one edge.
Roll each fillet up tightly into a thick log, tucking in the sides so the cheese stays inside.
Wrap each roll with two slices of bacon and tie with string or secure with toothpicks.

Brush with olive oil and cook over medium-low coals or on a grill pan for about 30 to 35 minutes, turning often, until the bacon is crisp and the chicken registers 74 C inside. Alternatively bake at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove the string and cut into thick slices to serve with salad or fries.

title: Pasta frola (Uruguayan jam tart with lattice top)

ingredients.name: quince paste, dulce de batata or thick jam, softened

steps: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder, zest and salt until it looks like fine crumbs.
Add the egg and yolk and bring together into a smooth dough without overworking. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 C. Roll out two-thirds of the dough and line a 24 cm tart tin, pressing it up the sides, and prick the base.
Warm the quince paste or jam briefly with a splash of water so it spreads, then spread it evenly over the dough.
Roll out the remaining dough, cut into strips and lay them over the filling in a lattice, pressing the ends onto the rim.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown. Cool in the tin before unmoulding and serve with mate or coffee.
